name: Huntington Bancshares Incorporated
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate regional-bank franchise: a sticky core deposit base and genuine relationship banking (Fair Play consumer brand, middle-market commercial relationships), Q2 2026 adjusted ROTCE 17.5% and OE positive 5 of last 5 FY on the legacy franchise — capped at weak-moderate because the product is commodity banking with no structural pricing power (management cut 2027 EPS guidance to $1.75–1.83 from $1.90–1.93 on September 16, 2026, citing funding costs and loan/deposit competition constraining NIM), full credit/rate-cycle exposure on a much larger loan book, CET1 down to 10.0% at Q2 2026, and two unintegrated acquisitions (Veritex closed Oct 2025, Cadence closed Feb 1, 2026 for roughly 462M new shares). A 4 gives CAP 7.2 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 8.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Solid super-regional bank, moat 4/10 — engine prints Tier B (weighted IRR 15.71%, IV@15% $15.94 vs $15.01) only by modelling the Cadence step-up into growth, so the final tier is softened to C at low confidence; it clears 15% with a margin of safety only below ~$12; bank-model mismatch, confidence low.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: a bank's OCF-based OE overstates distributable owner's earnings (loan growth consumes regulatory capital; provisions are a through-cycle cost OCF only partially carries), the weighted IRR of 15.71% clears the hurdle by only 0.71pp on a merger step-up assumption that has not survived a full audited combined year, and both other defensible runs print C (default preliminary 14.01%; TTM-base variant 12.74% on the share-count-distorted ttm.py base of $1.0623). Softened one notch, confidence low — same treatment as HIG/ACGL/ARES.
moat_for: Sticky core deposit franchise — deposits +37% YoY to $223.4B average in Q2 2026 (merger-assisted); local relationship banking, Midwest extended to Texas/South
Fair Play consumer brand — fee transparency (24-Hour Grace, Standby Cash, Early Pay) supports deposit retention in its markets
Scale step-up — ~$284B assets at Q2 2026, #1 deposit share in Mississippi, eighth-largest in Texas; payments/treasury/wealth/vehicle-finance fee businesses
Through-cycle profitability (legacy) — OE positive 5 of last 5 FY; Q2 2026 adjusted ROTCE 17.5%
Capital return restarting — planned 2027 repurchases raised to $1.3–1.4B (September 2026 update)
moat_against: Commodity product, no pricing power — 2027 EPS guide cut to $1.75–1.83 from $1.90–1.93 on funding costs and loan/deposit competition constraining NIM
Integration risk twice over — Veritex (Oct 2025) and Cadence (Feb 2026) unseasoned; $152M pretax acquisition notable items in Q2 2026 alone
Credit-cycle exposure — enlarged $189.3B average loan book assembled in a benign credit stretch; ACL 1.78% of loans at Q2 2026
Capital-constrained growth — CET1 10.0% at Q2 2026, down from 10.2% at Q1 2026; buybacks, loan growth and integration compete for capital
Per-share dilution to re-earn — ~462M shares issued for Cadence; earnings power depends on delivering $435M guided cost synergies
